{{nihongo|'''Usuki Hachiman Shrine'''|魚吹八幡神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} at Miyauchi 193, {{ill|Aboshi|Q11607184|qid=Q11607184}}, {{ill|Himeji|Q209801|qid=Q209801}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is also called "Tsu-no-miya." It is said to have been founded by divine oracle during {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}'s {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}. It is one of the candidate identifications for {{ill|Nakatomi Itate Shrine|Q17226544|qid=Q17226544}}, a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. {{nihongo|'''Usuki Hachiman Shrine'''|魚吹八幡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

A {{ill|Chikaraishi|Q1660393|qid=Q1660393}} said to have been lifted by {{ill|Sannomiya Unosuke|Q11354047|qid=Q11354047}} (an {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} strongman/acrobat) remains, and a statue of Unosuke is also erected.

== Festivals ==
* Bushin Festival - last Saturday of {{ill|March|Q110|qid=Q110}} (Himeji City designated intangible folk cultural property)
* Shokon Festival - April 22
* Sento Festival - {{ill|July 14|Q2691|qid=Q2691}}
* Autumn annual festival - {{ill|October 21|Q2960|qid=Q2960}}-{{ill|October 22|Q2957|qid=Q2957}}
== Lantern Festival ==
The autumn annual festival is called the '''Lantern Festival'''. Eighteen yatai, four danjiri, and one lion-danjiri participate; it has the largest number of parishioners in the Banshu region<ref>{{ill|Iwa Shrine (Matsumoto)|Q65320|qid=Q65320}}, the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of Harima, has 5 yatai; {{ill|Matsubara Hachiman Shrine|Q11529360|qid=Q11529360}} known for the {{ill|Nada no kenka matsuri|Q11566794|qid=Q11566794}} has 7; most other local shrines have single-digit counts, while Usuki has 23 total (yatai/danjiri/lion-danjiri).</ref>. It is one of the representative festivals of {{ill|Banshū Autumn Matsuri|Q11498705|qid=Q11498705}} and is designated an intangible folk cultural property of Hyogo Prefecture (2007).

The festival is said to originate from travel lanterns offered as sacred lights for three mikoshi carrying the three principal deities during their procession to the otabisho. After the war, it gradually became more intense, eventually featuring vigorous "neri" performances before shrine entry<ref>[https://www.himeji-kanko.jp/event/13 Lantern Festival <Usuki Hachiman Shrine>] Himeji Tourism Navi "Himenomichi"</ref>.
;Yoimiya (October 21)
The famous '''chochin neri''' crushes lanterns hung from tips of green bamboo poles about 3 meters long. From evening onward, this is performed by seven coastal districts in front of the romon and on the precinct approach. Other districts also hold yatai neri from daytime, with joint performances at sites including in front of JR {{ill|Aboshi Station|Q3611088|qid=Q3611088}} and {{ill|Katsuhara Elementary School|Q11447488|qid=Q11447488}}. Danjiri districts begin pulling danjiri toward the otabisho around noon. Around 22:00, three mikoshi and a gold gohei leave the main hall for the west otabisho ("Nishi no Baba") (togyo), where rites are performed (shinko-sai).
;Hirumiya (October 22)
From early morning, yatai and others from each district gather at the otabisho around 8-9 a.m. for joint neri. In the afternoon, mikoshi and gold gohei return to the shrine (kango), and yatai move to the shrine in prearranged order. Highlights include yatai neri lifting floats high with the shout "Chosa," lion dance, and danjiri performances.

At the 2019 hirumiya, before kango, a parade celebrating the emperor's accession was held in connection with that day's {{ill|Enthronement ceremony of the Japanese Emperor|Q20041008|qid=Q20041008}}.
;Festival areas
The following 24 towns:
* Himeji {{ill|Ōtsu|Q11437241|qid=Q11437241}} - '''Yoshimi''', '''Hiramatsu''', Temma, Nagamatsu, Nishi-doi
* Himeji {{ill|Katsuhara|Q11400189|qid=Q11400189}} - Asahi-dani, Kumami, Miyata, Yoro
* Himeji Aboshi Ward - '''Oeshima''', '''Kakichi''', '''Okinohama''', '''Shinzaike''', '''Yokohama''', Sakaide, Sakaue, Takada, Tsuichiba-kita, Tsuichiba, Fukui, Waku, Tai, Miyauchi
* {{ill|Ibo District, Hyōgo|Q1042150|qid=Q1042150}}{{ill|Taishi, Hyōgo|Q1155186|qid=Q1155186|lt=Taishi Town}} - Itoi

**Okinohama, Shinzaike, Yokohama, and Kakichi are danjiri districts; Asahi-dani is lion-danjiri. Miyauchi leads togyo/kango, and Waku with Ekimae conducts joint yatai procession. Other areas use yatai.
**Mikoshi and gold gohei assignments are fixed: Ojin by Okinohama, Jingu by Shinzaike, Tamayorihime by Yokohama, and gold gohei by Oeshima.
**'''Bold''' are the seven chochin-neri districts.

== Access ==
* 1 km north from {{ill|Sanyo-Aboshi Station|Q28812906|qid=Q28812906}} on {{ill|Sanyo Electric Railway|Q2245513|qid=Q2245513|lt=Sanyo Dentetsu}}.
* 2.5 km south from JR {{ill|Aboshi Station|Q3611088|qid=Q3611088|lt=Aboshi Station}} on {{ill|San'yō Main Line|Q1193436|qid=Q1193436}}; 5 minutes by taxi.
